//: Runway for abs_mu_jump.json (and the legacy config/ice_transition.json
//1: scripted demo): dry asphalt, then ice from x=0 onwards.
//3: The asphalt run-up has to be long enough for the whole PRE-brake half
//4: of the scenario -- reach entry speed AND settle off the throttle --
//5: before the vehicle reaches x=0.  It used to be 40 m spawn-to-boundary,
//6: which is about a third of what a ramped launch to 15 m/s needs, so the
//7: car crossed onto the ice at full throttle and the mu-jump this level
//8: exists for never happened: braking began 34 m past the boundary, i.e.
//9: entirely on ice.  Spawn to boundary is now 112 m.
//11: Budget, measured on this vehicle with the ramped launch in
//13: 0 -> 15 m/s        44.3 m   (entry speed at t = 7.72 s)
//15: brake on, asphalt   4.9 m   before the boundary
//18: The last line is deliberate and bounded.  Braking starts on asphalt,
//19: but only 4.9 m of it -- 42 % of the 11.6 m a stop from 14.29 m/s
//20: takes at this surface's own friction limit (v^2 / 2*0.9*g) -- so the
//21: car cannot stop before the ice however well ABS performs, and reaches
//22: the boundary at >= 10.9 m/s (24 mph) even in that best case.  What it
//23: actually crossed at, with no BTCM attached: 13.69 m/s (30.6 mph).
//24: Crossing under braking is the point -- this is the transition-braking
//25: test, and the transition belongs INSIDE the brake event.  What it must
//26: not be inside is the launch.
